chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, who said: Ahmad and Abdullah, the sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, narrated to me, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfaly, from Ali ibn Dawud al-Yaqubi, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Basri, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them.

That Ali (peace be upon him) said: There is no oath of condemnation (mula'ana) between five types of women and their spouses: a Jewish woman who is under a Muslim [husband]; a Christian woman and a slave woman who are under a free man, and he accuses them; a free woman who is under a slave [husband], and he accuses her; and a person who has been whipped for false accusation (li al-zina), because God, the Exalted, says: 'And do not accept their testimony ever.' And a dumb woman, there is no oath of condemnation between her and her husband; the oath of condemnation is by the tongue.

key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيَّةُ: A Christian woman, one of the categories exempt from Mula'ana when married to a Muslim.
key_terms.الْحُرِّ: A free man (as opposed to a slave), relevant to the marital status context.
key_terms.الْخُرْسَاءُ: A dumb woman, exempt because Mula'ana requires verbal oaths.
key_terms.الْفَرِيَّةُ: False accusation of adultery (li al-zina), specifically referring to the punishment of whipping.
key_terms.الْيَهُودِيَّةُ: A Jewish woman, one of the categories exempt from Mula'ana when married to a Muslim.
key_terms.بِاللِّسَانِ: By the tongue, indicating the verbal nature of the ritual.
key_terms.مُلاعَنَةٌ: Oath of condemnation, a ritual where spouses swear oaths to prove or disprove adultery.
key_terms.وَلَا تَقْبَلُوا لَهُمْ شَهَادَةً أَبَدً: Quranic verse meaning 'And do not accept their testimony ever', cited as the basis for the exemption.

ai.seo_question: What are the five exceptions to the Islamic ritual of Mula'ana (oath of condemnation) between spouses?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq to clarify the legal exceptions to *mula'ana*, emphasizing that the ritual requires verbal articulation, thereby excluding the deaf-mute (*kharsha*) and those whose testimony is permanently barred (*mardudah al-shahadah*) like the *majlud*. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential focus on the physical capacity to recite the specific oaths and the status of the parties involved, distinguishing these cases from the general rule of spousal accusation.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-84 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad and Abdullah - the sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Yazid al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Ali ibn Davood al-Yaqoobi, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Hafs al-Basry, on the authority of Aba Abdullah - Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his grandfather (MGB)

that Ali (MGB) said, “There can be no oath of condemnation between five types of women and their spouses: a Jewish woman and her Muslim husband; a Christian woman and her Muslim husband; a slave woman and her freed husband who claims that she has committed adultery; a freed woman who has a slave husband and claims that he has committed adultery; and a husband who has been punished for accusing his wife of having committed adultery as the Honorable the Exalted God says, ’… and reject their evidence ever after…’ ; and a dumb woman since she cannot take the oath of condemnation and it must be done verbally.”
